title: Picea orientalis
wikitext: {{Short description|Species of conifer}} {{Speciesbox | name = Caucasian spruce | image = Doğu ladini-1.jpg | image_caption = | status = LC | status_system = IUCN3.1 | status_ref = {{cite iucn |author=Farjon, A. |date=2013 |title=''Picea orientalis'' |volume=2013 |article-number=e.T42332A2973275 |doi=10.2305/IUCN.UK.2013-1.RLTS.T42332A2973275.en |access-date=19 November 2021}} | genus = Picea | species = orientalis | authority = ([[Carl Linnaeus|L.]]) [[Johann Heinrich Friedrich Link|Link]] | range_map = Picea orientalis range.svg | range_map_caption = {{Color box|#70A800}} Continuous range '''✖''' Isolated population }} '''''Picea orientalis''''', commonly known as the '''Oriental spruce''' or '''Caucasian spruce''',{{cite book |last1=Rushforth |first1=Keith D. |title=Conifers |publisher=Helm |publication-place=London |date=1987 |isbn=0-7470-2801-X |page=146}} is a [[species]] of [[spruce]] native to the [[Caucasus]] and adjacent northeast [[Turkey]]. ==Description== It is a large [[pinophyta|coniferous]] [[evergreen]] [[tree]] growing to {{convert|30|–|40|m|ft|0}} tall (exceptionally to 57 m),{{cite web |title=''Picea orientalis'' description |website=The Gymnosperm Database |date=2026-01-10 |url=https://www.conifers.org/pi/Picea_orientalis.php |access-date=2026-04-10}} and with a trunk diameter of up to 1.5 m (rarely up to 2.3 m). The shoots are buff-brown and moderately pubescent (hairy). The [[leaf|leaves]] are needle-like, the shortest of any spruce, 6–8 mm long, rhombic in cross-section, glossy dark green with inconspicuous [[stomata]]l lines. The [[conifer cone|cones]] are slender cylindric-conic, 5–9 cm long and 1.5 cm broad, green or red to purple when young, maturing dark brown 5–7 months after pollination, and have stiff, smoothly rounded scales.{{cite book |last=Farjon |first=Aljos |title=Pinaceae: drawings and descriptions of the genera ''Abies, Cedrus, Pseudolarix, Keteleeria, Nothotsuga, Tsuga, Cathaya, Pseudotsuga, Larix'' and ''Picea'' |publisher=Koeltz scientific books |publication-place=Königstein Champaign |date=1990 |isbn=3-87429-298-3 |pages=270–271}} ==Cultivation== It is a popular ornamental tree in large [[garden]]s, valued in northern Europe and the USA for its attractive foliage and ability to grow on a wide range of soils. It is also grown to a small extent in [[forestry]] for [[Christmas tree]]s, [[timber]] and [[paper]] production, though its slower growth compared to [[Norway spruce]] reduces its importance outside of its native range. ''P. orientalis''{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Picea orientalis''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/12969/Picea-orientalis/Details | access-date = 6 February 2021}} and the [[cultivar]]s 'Aurea' {{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/92725/Picea-orientalis-Aurea-(v)/Details | title = ''Picea orientalis'' 'Aurea' | publisher = RHS | access-date = 18 January 2021}} and 'Skylands'{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/82185/i-Picea-orientalis-i-Skylands/Details | title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Picea orientalis'' 'Skylands' | access-date = 25 April 2018}} have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 78 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 25 April 2018}} A frequently seen ornamental cultivar is ''Picea orientalis'' 'Aureospicata', which has gold-coloured young foliage in the spring.
